key_insight: Noise-biased qudits can make dynamical decoupling far more efficient, cutting the pulse overhead from quadratic to roughly linear in dimension while significantly extending coherence of nonclassical states.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to longer-lived logical qubits in higher-dimensional spin systems, improving the viability of resource-efficient quantum computing hardware.
method: Implemented dynamical decoupling on a model d=8 qudit: an antimony donor nuclear spin in silicon.
Exploited biased noise to reduce sequence overhead compared with standard qudit DD.
Benchmarked performance on uniform superpositions, cat states, Haar-random states, and a spin-cat code.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports coherence improvements of about 5–10×, with the logical |+>_L coherence extended to 225 ms versus 19 ms for free evolution and 85 ms for Hahn echo.
watch_item: The approach depends on strong noise bias and system-specific pulse design, so performance may not transfer directly to all qudit platforms.
paper_title: Dynamical Decoupling of Nonclassical States in a Biased-Noise Spin Qudit
